answer: Latency-Weighted Reputation Decay: each agent's voting weight grows with uninterrupted tenure and decays sharply on idle gaps, so identities must stay active across a long horizon to matter. New identities start near zero and gain slowly, while an attacker must fund sustained compute and uptime across a sprawling nebula of addresses, each isolated on its own island of activity. Cost scales with the square of parallel identities per unit time, making mass sybils economically self-defeating.
